document_check.note: Singh S, Malo PK, Stezin A, Menesgere AL, Issac TG. Hippocampal subfields volume changes and its correlation with memory functions in patients with mild cognitive impairment. Aging and Health Research 2024;4:100183. Cross-sectional comparison of 27 MCI patients and 36 controls from the CBR-TLSA cohort, Bangalore, India. Matches the cited study (Singh et al. 2024, South Asian cohort, subfield volume reductions).

cited_result: Lower hippocampal subfield volumes in MCI than in healthy controls (bilateral tail, subiculum, CA1, CA3, molecular layer; left presubiculum, parasubiculum, CA4, GC-ML-DG, HATA), GLM adjusted for age, sex and TIV; no whole-hippocampus comparison reported.
tool_reason: The cited result is a comparison of an imaging biomarker (subfield volume) between MCI patients and controls measured at one time point, which the brief assigns to the JBI analytical cross-sectional checklist.

domains.rationale: Criteria and setting are stated, but exclusions were asymmetric: only controls had to be free of chronic medical and psychiatric conditions, which favours a healthier control group and can widen group differences. The report does not say how the 63 imaged participants were chosen from the wider CBR-TLSA cohort, and education is not reported.

signalling.question: 1. Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: Inclusion criteria for the MCI group had memory impairment but not meet the criteria for dementia [1]. All the included participants with MCI had a clinical dementia rating (CDR) of 0.5 [14]. For healthy controls, CDR score was 0. Control participants were without any history of chronic medical or psychiatric conditions, or any previous history of head injury (e.g. concussions, trauma).

signalling.question: 2. Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: The participants were exclusively recruited from the Centre for Brain Research - Tata Longitudinal Study of Ageing (CBR-TLSA) project and were aged 45 years and above. The CBR-TLSA population comprises individuals who belong to a working, middle-class background in Bangalore city, Karnataka, India.

domains.domain: Exposure (diagnostic group) and condition criteria (JBI items 3 and 4)
domains.rationale: Here the exposure is diagnostic group membership and the condition is MCI. A CDR of 0.5 is a standard staging criterion. However, the report does not say how memory impairment was established: no test, cut-off or assessor is named, and it is not stated whether classification was blind to imaging.

signalling.question: 3. Was the exposure (MCI versus control group membership) measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: Inclusion criteria for the MCI group had memory impairment but not meet the criteria for dementia [1]. (I searched for the instrument, cut-off or assessor used to establish memory impairment and found none. ACE-III is described only as an outcome, not as a classification criterion.)

signalling.question: 4. Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: All the included participants with MCI had a clinical dementia rating (CDR) of 0.5 [14]. For healthy controls, CDR score was 0.

domains.rationale: Age, sex and total intracranial volume, the standard confounders for volumetric comparisons, were identified and entered as covariates in the GLM. Education was not considered, which matters less for volume than for cognition.

signalling.question: 5. Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: Additionally, GLM was used to investigate differences in hippocampal subfields volume while adjusting for age, sex, and TIV.

signalling.question: 6. Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: The hippocampal subfields volumes were extracted using Freesurfer software, and group differences and correlation were assessed using general linear model (GLM) with age, sex, and total intracranial volume (TIV) as covariates.

domains.rationale: Subfield volumes came from an established automated pipeline (FreeSurfer 7.2) run on a single 3T scanner with one protocol, with the segmentations checked visually. The unreliable alveus label was excluded. Small subfields segmented from 1 mm T1 images alone are less reliable, but this applies equally to both groups.

signalling.question: 7. Were the outcomes (subfield volumes) measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: The measurement of hippocampal subfield volumes for each participant was conducted using the Freesurfer software (v 7.2.0) ... a thorough examination of all processed data by an investigator was conducted, revealing no errors in the automatic labeling of participants.

domains.rationale: A GLM with covariates is an appropriate model. However, 24 subfield comparisons (12 per hemisphere) were each tested at an uncorrected p < 0.05 in a sample of 63, with no multiplicity correction. The list of individually significant subfields is therefore likely too long, although the overall pattern of lower volumes does not depend on any single test.

signalling.question: 8. Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: Additionally, GLM was used to investigate differences in hippocampal subfields volume while adjusting for age, sex, and TIV. ... Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05 (5% level of significance).

overall: Some concerns (JBI analytical cross-sectional: items 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 Yes; item 3 Unclear)
overall_rationale: Under the review's rule, none of the confounder, outcome-measurement or analysis items is No, but item 3 is Unclear, so the overall rating is some concerns. Beyond the checklist, three things weaken the result: the small convenience sample, exclusions that screened controls (but not patients) for chronic illness, and 24 uncorrected subfield tests. All of these make the exact list of affected subfields less certain than the general finding of lower subfield volumes in MCI.
